Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR adds an optional experimental PostgreSQL backend for Workboard while retaining SQLite as the default. **Example:** A new Workboard installation selects database.engine="postgres" and schemaPrefix="team". - **Before:** Workboard stores boards, cards, and attachments in SQLite. - **After:** Workboard stores them in a PostgreSQL schema named team_workboard_<store-id-prefix>, with a local SQLite identity anchor. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The approved architecture has substantial reported conformance coverage, but a reply-boundary defect and mandatory authority and upgrade verification prevent readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Operators cannot use PostgreSQL for Workboard persistence. **Reason:** The maintainer explicitly owns the experimental direction and its limits; the implementation retains one Workboard kernel and preserves SQLite as the default. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep this PR open: it delivers a maintainer-approved PostgreSQL pilot, but uncertain-write classification still breaks across Workboard replies. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: provide redacted terminal output or logs through a Workboard tool or Gateway method, storage worker, and real PostgreSQL client showing an allowed upload persists and an upload revoked during queueing or advisory-lock waiting is rejected before COMMIT; query physical blob and metadata rows to confirm the forbidden upload is absent. The reported conformance and connection-termination suites do not exercise this scenario. Also show a v2026.10.2 upgrade retaining populated SQLite Workboard data and settings. Redact credentials, IPs, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Preserve uncertain-outcome classification through Workboard replies (P2)** - When PostgreSQL loses its connection during COMMIT, the new write path throws a canonical SqliteWorkerError and this backend catches it into encodeWorkboardSqliteFailure. The outer worker then V8-serializes the envelope. The codec restores name and code but omits the private retainedWorkerErrorCode marker, so hasSqliteWorkerOutcomeUnknown on the host returns false even though the write may have committed. Preserve canonical classification explicitly across this envelope and cover a failure returned through createWorkboardSqliteStores, rather than only a direct PostgresSyncConnection call. This previously reported finding remains unresolved. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Verify revoked upload authority before PostgreSQL publication** - The new backend admits writes before advisory-lock waiting and requests host authority again before COMMIT. Existing upload tests skip PostgreSQL, so they do not establish rejection of a disabled upload at this final effect boundary or confirm physical blob and metadata cleanup. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - Establish that upload authority revoked during Workboard queueing or PostgreSQL advisory-lock waiting prevents durable blob and metadata publication. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Preserve uncertain-outcome classification through Workboard replies — `extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.worker.ts:158-159` - [medium] Verify revoked upload authority before PostgreSQL publication — `src/infra/postgres-sync/transaction.ts:59` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply a Workboard upload trace proving allowed persistence and rejection after revocation during queueing or PostgreSQL lock waiting, plus a v2026.10.2 upgrade preserving populated SQLite data and settings.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Workboard tools and Gateway methods submit storage operations to a worker; the selected SQL connection persists boards, cards, attachments, and session placements and publishes cache-invalidating receipts. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Workboard tools and Gateway] --> B[Workboard store] B --> C[Storage worker] C --> D[Shared Workboard kernel] D --> E[SQLite connection] D --> F[PostgreSQL bridge worker] F --> G[PostgreSQL schema] F --> H[SQLite identity anchor] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Preserve canonical uncertain-write errors through Workboard replies and verify the approved backend through upload-authority and stable-release upgrade scenarios. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the lost-marker path through Workboard's serialized error envelope; no runtime reproduction or target-code execution was performed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The shared Workboard kernel and worker-owned PostgreSQL client fit the approved pilot, but connection-level tests do not validate error classification across the Workboard reply boundary. Full review comments: - [P2] Preserve uncertain-outcome classification through Workboard replies — `extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.worker.ts:158-159` When PostgreSQL loses its connection during COMMIT, the new write path throws a canonical SqliteWorkerError and this backend catches it into encodeWorkboardSqliteFailure. The outer worker then V8-serializes the envelope. The codec restores name and code but omits the private retainedWorkerErrorCode marker, so hasSqliteWorkerOutcomeUnknown on the host returns false even though the write may have committed. Preserve canonical classification explicitly across this envelope and cover a failure returned through createWorkboardSqliteStores, rather than only a direct PostgresSyncConnection call. This previously reported finding remains unresolved. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.96 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [438e06c68838](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/438e06c68838bbc304c5552ba1e371b243677a7c). ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Hold for final-effect authority verification (recommended)** Keep this PR open until allowed uploads and uploads revoked during queueing or lock waiting are exercised through Workboard and the real PostgreSQL client, with physical persistence observations. ### Provenance checked - `Workboard storage and worker lifecycle` keeps the original intent (38fb08d04bd410122b4adcc5c1e43c54ed25b0b4: Move database work off the Gateway event loop while retaining data format, logical leases, draining, and retryable cleanup.) - `Transaction recovery` keeps the original intent (3d0254af02bacf51da80322a3b9e79fd8c4052c0: Retain terminal failures and refuse continuation after failed rollback; the new backend retires failed connections through its own connection owner.) - `PostgreSQL schema generation` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (457515502e84954c8061f9b151d63d92770d2a29: Generate a deterministic PostgreSQL projection from canonical SQLite schemas before runtime conformance; this maintainer-authored PR deliberately advances to a Workboard-only runtime pilot.) - `SQLite dialect ratchet` keeps the original intent (a1c1610b1907a3750f623297af19dedd425f7399: Prevent SQLite-specific SQL debt growth; the patch distinguishes portable savepoints and table column lists from engine-specific constructs.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security Needs attention: Upload revocation across the new PostgreSQL persistence boundary remains unverified; no concrete authorization bypass was established. ### Evidence Security concerns: - [medium] Verify revoked upload authority before PostgreSQL publication — `src/infra/postgres-sync/transaction.ts:59` The new backend admits writes before advisory-lock waiting and requests host authority again before COMMIT. Existing upload tests skip PostgreSQL, so they do not establish rejection of a disabled upload at this final effect boundary or confirm physical blob and metadata cleanup. Confidence: 0.92 What I checked: - **Approved direction and accepted pilot limits:** The maintainer-authored body explicitly selects an experimental Workboard-only backend, keeps SQLite as default, refuses engine switching for existing SQLite stores, requires paired backups, and accepts synchronous_commit=off. These choices do not require another product approval. ([`extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-schema.ts:335`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/438e06c68838bbc304c5552ba1e371b243677a7c/extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-schema.ts#L335), [438e06c68838](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/438e06c68838bbc304c5552ba1e371b243677a7c)) - **Uncertain errors lose canonical classification:** PostgreSQL connection loss creates a branded SqliteWorkerError. Workboard catches it inside its result envelope, serializes that envelope through V8, and restores ordinary error fields without restoring the private classification marker. ([`extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-errors.ts:25`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0/extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store-errors.ts#L25), [741fd94fb226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0)) - **Canonical checker requires the private marker:** hasSqliteWorkerOutcomeUnknown checks the retained symbol, including through causes and aggregates; an error's name and public code are insufficient. ([`src/infra/sqlite-worker-contract.ts:217`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0/src/infra/sqlite-worker-contract.ts#L217), [741fd94fb226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0)) - **Prior findings reassessed:** The new head adds the previously missing wrapper inventory entries. The Workboard uncertain-error codec is unchanged. ([`scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt:348`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0/scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt#L348), [741fd94fb226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0)) - **Authority coverage does not reach PostgreSQL upload persistence:** Existing upload-policy cases inspect physical SQLite rows and are skipped for PostgreSQL. ([`extensions/workboard/src/tools.upload-policy.test.ts:44`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0/extensions/workboard/src/tools.upload-policy.test.ts#L44), [741fd94fb226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/741fd94fb226118eb51013f90a76d0064711cbd0)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 457515502e84954c8061f9b151d63d92770d2a29 adds scripts/generate-postgres-schema.mts:14 relative to its recorded parents.
